# tree-sitter-starlark, vendored for sloplint

Date: 2026-10-20.

## Origin

Upstream repository: https://github.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-starlark.
Upstream tag: v1.3.0. Published crate: tree-sitter-starlark 1.3.0.
Name and version are unchanged.

This directory is the published crate plus the patch below.
README.md, LICENSE, `queries/`, `bindings/rust/`, and Cargo.toml are the
published files. `grammar.js` is patched.

## Why the published grammar reports a parse error on valid Starlark

Real Starlark has no `assert` statement. The Go implementation does not
reserve the name `assert`; its tests use a predeclared `assert` module, as
in `assert.eq(a, b)`. This python-derived grammar instead treats `assert`
as a keyword statement, with a hardcoded method set of eq, ne, contains
and fails. Valid code such as `assert.true(True)`, `assert.fail("x")`,
`assert.lt(a, b)` and `assert = module(...)` fails, while `x.true(True)`
parses. sloplint skips a whole file on any error node.

## Regenerating src/

Tool: tree-sitter-cli 0.27.1. JavaScript runtime: node v26.12.0.
Command, run in this directory: `tree-sitter generate`.
It rewrites `src/parser.c`, `src/grammar.json`, `src/node-types.json`
and `src/tree_sitter/*.h`. `src/scanner.c` is edited by hand and is not
generated; it is unchanged from the published crate.

`grammar.js` requires the tree-sitter-python grammar. Upstream pins
tree-sitter-python 0.23.5 in its lockfile, so generation resolves
`require('tree-sitter-python/grammar')` to that version, vendored here
under `node_modules/tree-sitter-python/` (grammar.js and LICENSE only).
The published `src/parser.c` was generated by tree-sitter-cli 0.24.4;
regenerating the unpatched grammar with 0.27.1 gives identical states
(2260), symbols (244) and trees on all 377 swept files, so the 0.27.1
output is a faithful baseline. The new parser targets ABI 15 instead of
14; the tree-sitter 0.27.1 runtime loads it.

## Changes to grammar.js

- New conflict: `[assert_statement, primary_expression]`. Same pattern
  as `print_statement` in the tree-sitter-python grammar.
- `assert_statement`: dropped the dotted builtin form
  (`assert.eq`, `assert.ne`, `assert.contains`, `assert.fails`).
  The statement keeps the six names `assert`, `assert_`, `assert_eq`,
  `assert_ne`, `assert_contains` and `assert_fails` as its keyword, with
  precedence prec(-3, dynamic -1).
- `keyword_identifier`: added the same six names. They now parse as
  identifiers, calls, subscripts and assignment targets.
- Net effect: when both readings fit (`assert(x)`, `assert[0]`,
  `assert - x`, `assert.eq(a, b)`), the ordinary reading wins. The
  Python-style statement `assert cond, message` stays accepted where it
  cannot be confused with an ordinary use.

## Changes to queries/highlights.scm

Removed the `(assert_builtin)` rule. That node no longer exists.
Kept the `(assert_keyword)` rule.

## Decision: the statement form is kept, not removed

The Starlark spec lists no assert statement, and the Go implementation
treats `assert` as an ordinary name. The statement form is still kept
for inputs where it cannot be confused, because the upstream corpus and
the existing sloplint `informative-assertions__starlark` fixture rely on
it, and removing it would turn those files into whole-file skips.
`sloplint-grammar.patch` and this file record the choice.

## Constructs verified fixed

Each was a parse error with the published crate and is valid Starlark:

- `assert.true(True)`
- `assert.fail("x")`
- `assert.lt(a, b)`
- `assert = module("assert", eq = _eq)` followed by `assert.eq(1, 1)`
- `assert_eq(a, b)`, `assert_fails(f, "msg")`, `assert_ = 1` as ordinary
  calls and assignment targets
- `assert(x)`, `assert[0]`, `assert - x` as ordinary expressions
- 30 swept files went from error to clean, including
  `starlarktest/assert.star` and the `starlark/testdata` files that use
  the `assert` module.

## Constructs known still failing

- Multi-chunk testdata files joined with `---` separators. One module
  per file is the input contract; `---` lines are invalid input.
- Deliberately invalid syntax cases in `syntax/testdata/errors.star`
  (each carries its own expected-error annotation) and in
  `resolve/testdata/resolve.star`.
- Two genuinely invalid real files: a truncated call in
  `INVALID.bazel` and a missing comma in a vendored `BUCK` file.

## Corpus results

Upstream `tree-sitter test` at tag v1.3.0, before the patch: 90 of 90
pass, plus 3 syntax-highlighting files. After the patch: 95 of 95 pass,
plus the same 3 highlighting files. New cases live in
`test/corpus/sloplint_assert.txt`: 5 cases (module calls, assert as a
name, helpers as calls and names, ambiguous forms, kept statement).
The unpatched grammar fails 3 of the 6 Rust regression tests; the
patched grammar passes all 6.

## Sweep result

Tree comparison between the published parser and this one on 377
`.star`, `.bzl`, `.bazel`, `BUILD`, `WORKSPACE` and `BUCK` files from
the cargo registry, the Go module cache, site-packages and
`~/compiler`: 30 files fixed, none broken, 320 trees identical.
7 clean files changed trees; each change only replaces an
`assert_statement` shape with the ordinary-identifier shape, proven
equal to the same file with `assert` renamed to a plain identifier
(70 of 70 files and chunks). A chunk-level sweep of the 21 multi-chunk
files (410 chunks) shows 14 chunks fixed, none broken, and 28 chunks
still erroring, all annotated as expected errors in the testdata.

## Size

`src/parser.c`: 2,490,275 bytes (published), 2,582,208 bytes (patched).
States: 2252 (patched) versus 2260 (published).
